item.title: A moderate earthquake shakes northeast Japan, injuring more than 20 in Tokyo region
item.summary: # A moderate earthquake shakes northeast Japan, injuring more than 20 in Tokyo region - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck eastern Japan early Sunday, jolting the Tokyo region, injuring more than 20 people and triggering emergency alerts but no tsunami warning, authorities said. - Most injuries occurred as residents were tossed from beds or stumbled in the dark; trains and airport links were briefly disrupted, a Tokyo water main burst, and hundreds lost power. TOKYO — A moderate earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.9 rattled eastern Japan, including the Tokyo area, early Sunday, injuring more than 20 people, most of them slightly, officials said. There was no danger of a tsunami. According to the Japan Meteorological Agency, the quake occurred in the southern Ibaraki prefecture, an area of Japan prone to frequent quakes, at a depth of 42 miles. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded a preliminary magnitude of 5.8. Twenty-three people were injured in four prefectures in the region — nine in Saitama, another nine in Kanagawa, four in Chiba and one in Ibaraki — according to prefectural officials.
